name: Question 2
problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,4,-2).$
worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the surface $z=f(x,y)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ on the surface can be written as

$$
z-{z}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\sqrt{y}-\frac{y}{2\sqrt{x}} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\sqrt{y}-y\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{x}{2\sqrt{y}}-\sqrt{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y)=(1,4):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4) & =\sqrt{4}-\frac{4}{2\sqrt{1}}=0 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{4}}-\sqrt{1}=-\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-(-2) & =(x-1)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(1,4)+(y-4)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(1,4) \\ z+2 & =0(x-1)-\frac{3}{4}(y-4) \\ z+2 & =-\frac{3}{4}y+3 \\ \frac{3}{4}y+z-1 & =0 \\ 3y+4z-4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
